newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's D'Alema says meeting with Kohl reassuring.
newsitem.headline: Italy's D'Alema says meeting with Kohl reassuring.

text.p: The leader of Italy's Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), Massimo D'Alema called a meeting on Thursday with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl "positive and reassuring" on the subject of economic and monetary union.

A statement from the PDS, the main party in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's ruling Olive Tree coalition, said D'Alema had met Kohl in Bonn on Thursday morning in a meeting that had been scheduled for several weeks.

"Regarding the newspaper reports relating to the process of European monetary union which are currently occupying Italian public opinion, the talk with the Chancellor were positive and reassuring," the statement said.
On Wednesday, the Financial Times daily reported that a plan was being prepared to get Italy to delay its entry into a single European currency at its projected 1999 start.
The existence of such a plan was denied by Bonn, Brussels and Rome and Prodi reiterated Italy's determination to meet economic and monetary union criteria.
Prodi is due to meet Kohl in Bonn on Friday.
